claims.text: Nb-Mo-Ta-W-V-Ti can be synthesized by mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering.
Ball milling the NbMoTaWVTi powder for 40 hours produces two BCC solid solutions.
Mechanical alloying produces grain refinement through severe plastic deformation.
Mechanical alloying and SPS can retain a grain size below 50 nm in bulk NbMoTaWVTi.
SPS consolidation of mechanically alloyed NbMoTaWVTi produces an FCC precipitated phase in a BCC matrix.
The FCC precipitate in SPS-consolidated NbMoTaWVTi can be TiO introduced through oxygen contamination during preparation.
The BCC matrix plus FCC TiO precipitates constitute a dual-phase solid-solution structure.
SPS at 1000-1200 degrees Celsius retains the sub-50 nm grain structure and promotes the desired dual-phase constitution.
Processing under argon prevents oxidation during preparation and consolidation.
Fine BCC grains strengthen the consolidated alloy through grain-boundary strengthening.
TiO particles strengthen the consolidated alloy through precipitation strengthening.
The proposed NbMoTaWVTi material can have hardness above 10 GPa.
The consolidated NbMoTaWVTi alloy can have yield strength above 2.5 GPa.
The consolidated NbMoTaWVTi alloy can have total fracture strain above 10%.
The proposed processing route avoids brittle intermetallic phases.
Cast NbMoTaWVTi has limited ductility because of brittle BCC phases and intermetallic formation.
The nanocrystalline dual-phase structure becomes unstable above 1200 degrees Celsius because of grain growth and phase decomposition.
Mechanical alloying for more than 60 hours may cause amorphization or excessive defect accumulation and reduce ductility.
Sintering at 1400 degrees Celsius should produce coarser grains, loss of FCC precipitates, and reduced mechanical properties relative to the optimized process.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify an inert atmosphere to prevent oxidation, while the proposed FCC strengthening phase is TiO whose formation is attributed to oxygen introduced during preparation.
The target constitution is called a dual-phase solid-solution structure, but the identified FCC phase is TiO, a separate oxide precipitate rather than an FCC metallic solid solution.
